verses.1: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of the Medes' lineage, who became king over the Chaldean kingdom,
verses.2: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years that the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah the prophet for the fulfillment of the desolation of Jerusalem—seventy years.
verses.3: So I turned my face to the Lord God, to seek prayer and entreaties, in fasting and sackcloth.
verses.4: I prayed to the Lord my God and confessed, saying, "O Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and steadfast love for those who love You and keep Your commandments,
verses.5: we have sinned and done wrong, been wicked and rebellious, turning away from Your commandments and Your laws,
verses.6: and we have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, our officials, our fathers, and all the people of the land.
verses.7: To You, Lord, belongs the righteousness, and to us the shame of face, this day to every man of Judah, to those living in Jerusalem, and to all Israel, near and far in every land where You have scattered them because of their rebellion in which they rebelled against You.
verses.8: To You, Lord, belongs our shame of face, to our kings, our officials, and our fathers, who sinned against You.
verses.9: To the Lord, our God, belong mercy and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against Him.
verses.10: And we have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God to walk in His teachings that He set before us by His servants the prophets.
verses.11: And all Israel has transgressed Your law and turned away from listening to Your voice. And You have brought upon us the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses, Your servant, because we have sinned against Him.
verses.12: And He has fulfilled His words that He spoke over us and over our judges who judged us, bringing upon us great calamity, such as never happened under the entire heavens as it has happened in Jerusalem.
verses.13: As it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil has come upon us, yet we did not turn our faces to the Lord our God to return from our iniquity and to know Your truth.
verses.14: And the Lord has watched over the evil and has brought it upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in all His works that He has done, and we did not listen to His voice.
verses.15: And now, Lord, our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made for Yourself a name as this day—we have sinned, we have done wrong.
verses.16: O Lord, by all Your righteousness, let now Your anger and Your wrath turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain, for because of our sins and the sins of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people have become a disgrace to all those around us.
verses.17: And now, Lord our God, listen to the prayer of Your servant and to his entreaties, and let Your face shine upon Your desolate sanctuary for Your sake, Lord.
verses.18: Incline Your ear, my God, and hear. Open Your eyes and see our desolations and the city that is called by Your name, for it is not by our righteousness that we are casting our plea before You, but by Your great mercies.
verses.19: O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, attend and act! Do not delay, for Your name is called upon Your city and upon Your people.
verses.20: And while I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and casting my plea before the Lord my God for the holy mountain of my God,
verses.21: while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, flew swiftly and touched me at the time of the evening sacrifice.
verses.22: He instructed me and spoke with me, saying, "Daniel, now I have come to make you understand wisdom.
verses.23: At the beginning of your entreaties, the word went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are a man of desires, and you have understood the word and comprehend the vision.
verses.24: Seventy weeks are cut off for your people and for your holy city, to finish the transgression, to put an end to sins, to atone for wickedness, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy.
verses.25: And you will know and understand: from the going out of the word to restore and to build Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the Prince, there are seven weeks. Then for sixty-two weeks it will be rebuilt with streets and moats, even in the time of distress.
verses.26: And after the sixty-two weeks, the Anointed One will be cut off, and there will be no inheritance for him. And the city and the holy place will be destroyed by the leader who comes; his end will be with a flood, and until the end of the war desolations are determined.
verses.27: And he will confirm a covenant for many for one week. And in the middle of the week, he will cause the sacrifice and offering to cease, and on the wing of abominations he will make it desolate, even until the end, and a decree of destruction will be poured out on the desolation."

notes:
Notes
- v. 24: "Seventy weeks" refers to the unit "week" as a period of seven years, a common interpretive assumption in Jewish apocalyptic literature, not a literal seven days.
- v. 25: "Anointed One, the Prince" translates "meshiach nagid," typically rendered as "Messiah, the Prince" in English.
- v. 26: "the Anointed One will be cut off" uses "cut off" as a common metaphor for death or removal, in line with the context.
- v. 27: "in the middle of the week" refers to the midpoint of the final seven-year period, often interpreted as a key eschatological event.
- v. 27: "abominations" as in "wing of abominations" translates "shiqqutzim," a term with strong negative connotations, often associated with detestable or idolatrous practices.

[1] In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of the Medes' lineage, who became king over the Chaldean kingdom,
[2] in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years that the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah the prophet for the fulfillment of the desolation of Jerusalem—seventy years.
[3] So I turned my face to the Lord God, to seek prayer and entreaties, in fasting and sackcloth.
[4] I prayed to the Lord my God and confessed, saying, "O Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and steadfast love for those who love You and keep Your commandments,
[5] we have sinned and done wrong, been wicked and rebellious, turning away from Your commandments and Your laws,
[6] and we have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, our officials, our fathers, and all the people of the land.
[7] To You, Lord, belongs the righteousness, and to us the shame of face, this day to every man of Judah, to those living in Jerusalem, and to all Israel, near and far in every land where You have scattered them because of their rebellion in which they rebelled against You.
[8] To You, Lord, belongs our shame of face, to our kings, our officials, and our fathers, who sinned against You.
[9] To the Lord, our God, belong mercy and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against Him.
[10] And we have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God to walk in His teachings that He set before us by His servants the prophets.
[11] And all Israel has transgressed Your law and turned away from listening to Your voice. And You have brought upon us the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses, Your servant, because we have sinned against Him.
[12] And He has fulfilled His words that He spoke over us and over our judges who judged us, bringing upon us great calamity, such as never happened under the entire heavens as it has happened in Jerusalem.
[13] As it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil has come upon us, yet we did not turn our faces to the Lord our God to return from our iniquity and to know Your truth.
[14] And the Lord has watched over the evil and has brought it upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in all His works that He has done, and we did not listen to His voice.
[15] And now, Lord, our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made for Yourself a name as this day—we have sinned, we have done wrong.
[16] O Lord, by all Your righteousness, let now Your anger and Your wrath turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain, for because of our sins and the sins of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people have become a disgrace to all those around us.
[17] And now, Lord our God, listen to the prayer of Your servant and to his entreaties, and let Your face shine upon Your desolate sanctuary for Your sake, Lord.
[18] Incline Your ear, my God, and hear. Open Your eyes and see our desolations and the city that is called by Your name, for it is not by our righteousness that we are casting our plea before You, but by Your great mercies.
[19] O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, attend and act! Do not delay, for Your name is called upon Your city and upon Your people.
[20] And while I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and casting my plea before the Lord my God for the holy mountain of my God,
[21] while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, flew swiftly and touched me at the time of the evening sacrifice.
[22] He instructed me and spoke with me, saying, "Daniel, now I have come to make you understand wisdom.
[23] At the beginning of your entreaties, the word went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are a man of desires, and you have understood the word and comprehend the vision.
[24] Seventy weeks are cut off for your people and for your holy city, to finish the transgression, to put an end to sins, to atone for wickedness, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy.
[25] And you will know and understand: from the going out of the word to restore and to build Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the Prince, there are seven weeks. Then for sixty-two weeks it will be rebuilt with streets and moats, even in the time of distress.
[26] And after the sixty-two weeks, the Anointed One will be cut off, and there will be no inheritance for him. And the city and the holy place will be destroyed by the leader who comes; his end will be with a flood, and until the end of the war desolations are determined.
[27] And he will confirm a covenant for many for one week. And in the middle of the week, he will cause the sacrifice and offering to cease, and on the wing of abominations he will make it desolate, even until the end, and a decree of destruction will be poured out on the desolation."
